subject: MemoryVault suspected exfiltration — IR alignment and evidence request
messages:
From: Alice Turner <alice.turner@memoryvault.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@memoryvault.com
Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Unusual access to archived tenant logs — quick sync?

Hi Mina,

Apologies for the early note. Our platform monitoring flagged an abnormal pattern of list/get operations against an archived S3 bucket that contains paired telemetry for one of our tenants that uses Redwood. The activity window is 2027-10-17 22:30–23:05 UTC and looks like several short-lived sessions from an IP range we don't recognize.

We believe this may be a limited exfiltration attempt; nothing obvious yet (no large downloads) but we want to be thorough. Can you confirm whether any Redwood processes (backups, analytics jobs, reindexing, or scheduled exports) would have accessed MemoryVault tenant data during that window?

If possible, we need: 1) a copy of any S3 access logs referencing the MemoryVault tenant for that interval, 2) the list of Redwood service identities that could have inbound access to that bucket, and 3) whether any IR playbook steps were triggered on your side.

We are beginning an internal containment assessment but wanted to coordinate quickly in case you have additional telemetry. I'll loop in our SOC if we need longer retention for artifacts.

Attachments: memoryvault-s3-access-logs.csv (CSV, 4.2MB) — extracted from our CloudTrail export.

Thanks,
Alice Turner
Sr. Security Engineer
MemoryVault
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@memoryvault.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2027 09:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unusual access to archived tenant logs — quick sync?

Alice — thanks for the heads up and for the logs. We take this seriously. Short answers up front:

- No scheduled backup/export jobs map to MemoryVault's tenant in that window. Our nightly analytics job ran earlier in the evening and completed at ~20:45 UTC.
- I see three Redwood service principals that could interact with S3: redwood-telemetry-worker, redwood-log-archiver, and redwood-telemetry-ingest; preliminary access audit shows redwood-log-archiver initiated a HEAD/GET sequence earlier the same day but not from unfamiliar IPs.

I'm looping in Marissa (Security Ops) for evidence collection and Karthik for IR playbook activation and retention policy overrides. Grace — can you stand up an evidence export (full access logs, instance metadata, and any k/v cache eviction traces) and put it on a shared drive with the MemoryVault label? We will need the export preserved for 90 days while the investigation is ongoing.

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa to coordinate mutual action plan and evidence handoff (today EOD)
- Karthik to confirm whether we should initiate our IR runbook (weighing scope vs. provider notice)
- Mina to review our infra routing and verify no internal misconfig that would expose tenant S3 beyond known service principals

Please confirm if MemoryVault needs an accelerated NDA for deeper artifacts; otherwise we'll share sanitized artifacts first and escalate if you need full headers and instance identifiers.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Head of Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference

Alice / team — I pulled the artifacts requested and staged them in Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/MemoryVault/IR/evidence-2027-10-18

Contents:
- memoryvault-s3-access-logs.csv (original from MemoryVault)
- redwood-s3-server-logs-20271017-22-00-to-23-30.csv (our S3 access logs)
- ec2-instance-metadata-20271017.json (instance identities that made S3 calls)
- redwood-service-principals-2027-10.csv (trimmed list of service principals with recent S3 permissions)

Please note: we redacted full instance hostnames in the staged CSV per our privacy policy. If you need the unredacted hostnames for law enforcement or deeper forensics, we will require a formal request via your legal/soc team and a mutual CIIA/NDA addendum.

Karthik — recommend we run containment steps from section 3 of the IR playbook (rotate affected keys, snap EBS, and block the suspect IP range) and trigger a brief canary to validate no further traffic flows. Are you OK to take operational lead?

Alice — if you can call out specific artifacts you want unredacted in reply, we will prioritize.

Attachments: ir_timeline-draft.pdf (PDF, 220KB)

—Marissa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Alice Turner <alice.turner@memoryvault.com>, security@memoryvault.com, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Oct 2027 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Unusual access to archived tenant logs — postmortem and closure items

Team / Alice — quick update and postmortem deliverable. Summary: we executed containment steps at 2027-10-18T23:05:30Z (blocked IP range and rotated the short-lived service key used by redwood-log-archiver). Nothing in the staged logs indicates mass download beyond the CSV MemoryVault shared; timeline indicates an opportunistic HEAD/GET pattern but no sustained data transfer.

What we uploaded to the shared Drive (link above) now includes: postmortem-memoryvault-10-19-2027.pdf (final), a forensics manifest, and a sanitized packet capture for the suspect sessions. We kept a sealed copy of unredacted host identifiers and full EBS snapshots in our secure evidence vault; request from MemoryVault legal or law enforcement required to release.

SOC2/SIG/CAIQ context: items extracted for your SOC team in the postmortem are labeled to map to the SIG (v2027) controls and our SOC 2 control IDs. If the MemoryVault compliance team would like a CAIQ crosswalk we can generate one (estimated 3 business days) — let us know.

Open asks:
- Alice: please confirm whether you consider this a reportable incident in your environment (we will mirror your reporting cadence).
- MemoryVault legal: if you require full hostnames/EBS snapshots, open a formal request so we can provision an export with chain-of-custody.
- Grace: please confirm evidence retention extension to 90 days and mark artifacts as pending litigation hold in the vault.

I'll close the IR ticket once I get confirmation on reporting status from MemoryVault and retention OK from Grace.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Incident Response
Redwood Inference
